title: Adaptive KV anchoring and per-sequence profile publishing for model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an adaptive KV anchoring mechanism and a per-sequence performance profile publishing flow to improve long-context performance for newly onboarded model versions. The goal is to automatically select an initial KV retention/eviction anchor for a model-version based on sampled sequence clusters and to publish a validated profile that downstream routing and runtime components can consume.
background: We often see wide variance in KV cache effectiveness across model versions and customer sequence distributions. Current onboarding requires manual tuning or broad conservative defaults that either waste memory or underperform for long-context workloads. Prior tickets created per-model sequence histograms and pinning guidance, but lack a lightweight anchored default and an automated publishable profile that integrates with version rollouts.
goals: 1) Generate a deterministic per-model-version anchor suggestion from sampled sequence clusters. 2) Validate anchor against a short canary pass on a shadow runtime to measure hit-rate and latency delta. 3) Publish a profile JSON to the profile registry that routing, autoscaler, and the onboarding UI can consume.
scope: - Sampling pipeline: collect representative sequence length clusters during onboarding ingestion. - Anchor heuristic: compute anchor retention window and eviction thresholds. - Canary validation runner: shadow validation against a small traffic sample. - Profile publishing: register profile metadata, metrics baseline, and recommended default anchor. Excludes UI changes beyond a small onboarding banner and does not change autoscaling logic in this ticket.
tasks: Add sequence-cluster sampler to onboarding job (batch/stream modes)
Implement anchor heuristic: weighted percentile + tail-sensitivity factor
Create canary validation runner that runs on dedicated small GPU pool
Define profile JSON schema and registry API contract
Integrate publish step into onboarding workflow with retry/backoff
Add telemetry hooks: pre/post canary latency, kv-hit-rate, memory delta
Write unit/integration tests and an end-to-end smoke canary
Document expected profile fields for PM/Console usage
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding job produces a candidate anchor for 95% of model-version inputs within the sample budget
Canary runner reports latency delta and kv hit rate; candidate marked as 'validated' if latency regression < 5% and kv hit-rate > baseline + 3%
Profile registry accepts the published profile and the console can display the anchor suggestion for the version
Telemetry emitted to the runtime metrics pipeline and dashboards for the canary and first-week post-publish
Automated rollback: if live traffic shows a regression above thresholds, profile publish is flagged and an auto-fallback to conservative anchor occurs
design_tradeoffs: We choose a lightweight anchor heuristic (percentile + tail multiplier) to avoid expensive per-sequence optimization during onboarding. This sacrifices some per-customer optimality but enables fast onboarding and deterministic behavior. A more aggressive ML-driven anchor predictor was considered but deferred due to data/labeling cost and release complexity.
testing_plan: Unit tests for sampling and heuristic. Integration tests for publish API with a mocked registry. Canary validation will run against a replay dataset and then a shadow live sample on a non-production GPU pool. Performance tests will measure kv hit-rate, memory usage, and p50/p95 latency with and without anchor applied.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature behind a runtime feature flag. 2) Run onboarding for a selected set of low-risk models (internal + opt-in customers). 3) Monitor canary dashboards for 72 hours. 4) Gradually enable by default for all onboarding pipelines if stable. 5) Post-rollout retrospective and possible tuning iteration.
risks: Anchor heuristic could select suboptimal retention for long-tail sequences causing latencies to increase
Canary sample may not reflect production distribution leading to false validation
Profile publish API changes could break downstream consumers if schema incompatible
Memory footprint growth for models with incorrect anchors could pressure dedicated pools
